title: Bundibugyo virus disease in outbreak settings: A practical clinical review

analysis.scope_and_question: Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) is a severe filovirus infection caused by Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), an orthoebolavirus with diagnostic and countermeasure implications distinct from Ebola virus (EBOV).
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has expanded substantially, with 7890 confirmed cases and 3799 deaths reported across 63 health zones in seven provinces as of 23 September 2026.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: BVD usually presents as a nonspecific febrile and gastrointestinal illness; haemorrhagic manifestations are uncommon at presentation. No vaccine or specific therapeutic has established clinical efficacy against BDBV in humans; Ervebo is being evaluated within research protocols and the PARTNERS trial is evaluating MBP134 and remdesivir-based regimens.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Early outbreak investigation also showed that EBOV-oriented testing can fail to detect BDBV, making species-appropriate molecular testing essential when BDBV is epidemiologically plausible. Insecurity, displacement, laboratory and transport constraints, and delayed presentation continue to limit implementation.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Supportive care remains the standard of management, but what can be delivered safely differs between peripheral facilities and dedicated filovirus treatment centres. First-contact facilities should prioritise recognition, separation, protected sampling, treatment of immediately life-threatening or common treatable conditions, and early referral; treatment centres can provide closer monitoring, advanced supportive care, and access to approved research protocols.

analysis.summary_en: This review focuses on Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD), a severe filovirus infection caused by Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), an orthoebolavirus distinct from Ebola virus (EBOV). It highlights the clinical presentation of BVD as a nonspecific febrile and gastrointestinal illness, with rare haemorrhagic manifestations. The ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has reported 7890 confirmed cases and 3799 deaths as of 23 September 2026. The review emphasizes the importance of species-appropriate molecular testing for BDBV, as EBOV-oriented tests may fail to detect it. It also outlines the limitations in outbreak management due to insecurity, displacement, and logistical challenges. Currently, no vaccine or specific therapeutic has established clinical efficacy against BDBV, with Ervebo and the PARTNERS trial evaluating potential treatments. The review underscores the need for tailored supportive care, with peripheral facilities focusing on immediate life-threatening conditions and early referral, while dedicated treatment centres provide advanced care and access to research protocols.

title: Adaptation of Bayesian decision analysis for clinical trial design to binary outcomes: illustration for Ebola virus disease treatment.

analysis.research_question_and_background: When designing trials for high-mortality diseases with limited therapies, the conventional 5% type I error rate (α) may be unsuitable. A higher α could benefit seriously ill patients lacking therapeutic alternatives.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We consider fixed, two-arm randomized trials with binary outcomes and two types of clinical trial losses: post-trial loss, for not approving an effective treatment or approving an ineffective one; in-trial loss, for not administrating an effective treatment to control-arm patients or for administrating an ineffective treatment to experimental-arm patients.
analysis.methods: Bayesian decision analysis (BDA) integrates multiple health consequences into trial design. Using mortality as the outcome, we modeled various epidemic scenarios by varying target population size, mortality rate, and treatment efficacy.
analysis.main_results: In most cases, BDA-optimal α exceeded the conventional one-sided 2.5% and sample sizes are smaller. Simulations comparing BDA-optimized two-arm trials (fixed/sequential) to conventional designs (two-arm/single-arm, fixed/sequential) across outbreak scenarios show comparable statistical power across designs, except when sample size assumptions are incorrect, or when trials started after the outbreak peak; in these situations, BDA-optimized trials show superior powers.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The model incorporates treatment side effects and disease severity into a single loss function, from which BDA-optimal n and α are derived. This BDA framework provides a promising approach for designing trials with binary outcomes, particularly in high-mortality disease outbreaks, where declining case numbers and uncertain mortality and efficacy data challenge conventional methods.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings cautiously inform the design of clinical trials for high-mortality diseases, particularly Ebola virus disease, by providing a method to optimize sample sizes and type I error rates based on multiple health consequences.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The model assumes fixed, two-arm randomized trials and does not account for all possible clinical trial losses. The evidence strength is moderate due to the assumptions and limitations of the model.

analysis.summary_en: The study developed a Bayesian decision analysis (BDA) framework to optimize sample sizes and type I error rates for clinical trials of high-mortality diseases, particularly Ebola virus disease, by integrating multiple health consequences into trial design.

title: Early detection of immunoglobulin A against a vaccine backbone protein enables fast, durable, and objective identification of individuals vaccinated against Ebola virus.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the challenge of distinguishing between individuals vaccinated against Ebola virus and those previously infected, as current diagnostic assays lack reliability in this regard. The background highlights that the rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP vaccine is recommended for preventing Ebola virus infection and disease, yet breakthrough infections have been observed in vaccinees.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated longitudinal samples from 30 individuals vaccinated with rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP and 30 placebo recipients, along with 8 participants from a long-term vaccination follow-up study. The design focused on analyzing immune responses over time to assess vaccine-induced immunity.
analysis.methods: A multiplex sero-diagnostic assay was developed to detect IgA, IgG, and IgM antibodies against VSV-N, a vaccine-specific marker absent in natural infection, and EBOV-GP, the vaccine's target antigen. The assay was applied to the longitudinal samples to measure antibody responses.
analysis.main_results: The assay detected an increase in all antibodies against both protein antigens in vaccinated individuals. Critically, anti-VSV-N IgA responses emerged earlier and more robustly than anti-GP responses, establishing anti-N IgA as a durable biomarker of vaccination with high sensitivity and specificity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The assay enables rapid, accurate identification of vaccine recipients and supports real-time assessment of vaccine effectiveness during outbreaks. It also positions as a transformative platform for future infectious disease preparedness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide a reliable method for differentiating vaccine-induced immunity from natural infection, which is crucial for vaccine-effectiveness studies, seroepidemiologic investigations, and accurate outbreak response strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on longitudinal samples from a specific cohort, which may affect generalizability. However, the evidence is strong, with clear, high-sensitivity and high-specificity results supporting the assay's utility.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to address the challenge of distinguishing between individuals vaccinated against Ebola virus and those previously infected, as current diagnostic assays lack reliability. The researchers developed a multiplex sero-diagnostic assay to detect IgA, IgG, and IgM antibodies against VSV-N, a vaccine-specific marker, and EBOV-GP, the vaccine's target antigen. They evaluated longitudinal samples from 30 vaccinated individuals, 30 placebo recipients, and 8 participants from a long-term follow-up study. The assay detected increased antibody levels in vaccinated individuals, with anti-VSV-N IgA responses emerging earlier and more robustly than anti-GP responses, establishing it as a durable biomarker of vaccination. The findings suggest that this assay can enable rapid, accurate identification of vaccine recipients and support real-time assessment of vaccine effectiveness during outbreaks. The study's results are strong, with high sensitivity and specificity, but its reliance on a specific cohort may limit generalizability.

title: Cross-border preparedness, health worker protection, and institutional response in the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the international response to the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda, examining cross-border preparedness under the amended IHR and WHO Pandemic Agreement, frontline health worker protection, and institutional response and research investment. The central question is how these factors influenced the management of the outbreak and what lessons can be drawn for future preparedness.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a Perspective rather than a systematic assessment of the evidence. It does not report on databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, or study counts. The author presents an analytical position on the international response to the BVD outbreak, without conducting a meta-analysis or consensus process.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that genuine early action coexisted with significant weaknesses in cross-border screening coordination, healthcare worker protection, and community engagement. It concludes that these gaps reflect governance weaknesses, financing shortfalls, and insecurity rather than any single cause. The absence of a licensed, Bundibugyo-specific vaccine or therapeutic is noted as a critical institutional response issue.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies gaps in healthcare worker protection and cross-border coordination as key controversies. It also notes the limited community engagement, exemplified by the burning of an Ebola treatment centre in Rwampara, which suggests unresolved challenges in public health communication and trust-building. The evidence does not provide a comprehensive analysis of these issues, leaving them as unresolved gaps.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review recommends cross-border surveillance protocols, improved healthcare worker protection, enhanced community engagement, and equitable research investment in neglected pathogens. These recommendations are directed at policymakers, Africa CDC, WHO, and practitioners to strengthen future responses to similar outbreaks.

analysis.summary_en: This review analyzes the international response to the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda. It highlights cross-border preparedness under the amended IHR and WHO Pandemic Agreement, frontline health worker protection, and institutional response challenges. The review notes the absence of a licensed vaccine or therapy for BVD and the burning of an Ebola treatment centre in Rwampara as examples of governance and community engagement failures. It concludes that these gaps reflect systemic issues rather than isolated causes. The review recommends improved surveillance, healthcare worker safety, community engagement, and equitable research investment to address these challenges and enhance future outbreak responses.

title: Longitudinal Filovirus Seroreactivity Following Ad26.ZEBOV (Zabdeno) and MVA-BN-Filo (Mvabea) Vaccination in the Democratic Republic of the Congo

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess the long-term immunogenicity of the Ad26.ZEBOV/MVA-BN-Filo vaccine in a population in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), where filovirus seroreactivity is prevalent. The research addressed the need for real-world data on the vaccine's efficacy, given limited existing data.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in Mbandaka, Equateur province, DRC, from September 2023 to October 2024. It involved 698 participants who were assessed for seroreactivity to six filovirus antigens at three timepoints: baseline, 6-8 weeks post-first dose, and one year post-booster dose.
analysis.methods: Seroreactivity was assessed using a multiplexed immunoassay. Samples were collected from individuals who had received the Ad26.ZEBOV/MVA-BN-Filo vaccine regimen, which includes the MVA-BN-Filo booster dose containing EBOV, MARV, and SUDV GP and nucleoprotein from Tai Forest virus.
analysis.main_results: At baseline, 48.7% of participants were seroreactive to at least one filovirus antigen. EBOV GP seroreactivity increased to 66.8% one year post-booster dose, while there were no substantial increases in reactivity against SUDV GP and MARV GP. Overall filovirus seroreactivity increased at all timepoints, but decreased for those seroreactive at baseline.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that the Ad26.ZEBOV/MVA-BN-Filo vaccine induces stable seroreactivity against EBOV GP, but not to other filovirus antigens. High baseline seroreactivity to BDBV GP was also observed, despite no previous documented outbreaks in the region.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that the vaccine is effective in inducing long-term seroreactivity against EBOV GP, which is crucial for surveillance and early detection of EBOV outbreaks. However, the lack of increased reactivity against other filovirus antigens indicates the need for additional vaccines or booster strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's design limitations include the lack of a control group and the potential for confounding factors. The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational nature of the study and the limited sample size.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the long-term immunogenicity of the Ad26.ZEBOV/MVA-BN-Filo vaccine in the DRC, finding stable seroreactivity against EBOV GP but not other filovirus antigens. High baseline seroreactivity to BDBV GP was also observed.

title: Ebola Virus Disease in Pregnancy: Maternal–Fetal Outcomes, Vertical Transmission, and Implications for Vaccination—A Narrative Review

analysis.scope_and_question: Background/Objectives: Ebola virus disease (EVD) during pregnancy is associated with severe maternal illness and exceptionally poor fetal and neonatal outcomes.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched from inception through May 2026 using predefined terms related to EVD, pregnancy, maternal and neonatal outcomes, placental infection, vertical transmission, and vaccination.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Historical reports documented very high maternal mortality and pregnancy loss; however, more recent studies do not indicate that pregnancy independently increases maternal mortality among patients with EVD.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: However, pregnancy-specific evidence remains limited by small cohorts, heterogeneous outbreak settings, and the historical exclusion of pregnant women from clinical research.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on maternal, fetal, and neonatal outcomes, placental involvement and vertical transmission, clinical management, and vaccination during pregnancy.

analysis.summary_en: This review synthesizes evidence on maternal, fetal, and neonatal outcomes of Ebola virus disease during pregnancy, highlighting substantial pregnancy loss and neonatal mortality despite improved maternal care. The review also identifies gaps in understanding maternal-fetal transmission and long-term infant outcomes, emphasizing the need for further research.

title: Identification of Host Gene Transcripts by Machine Learning and Their Application to Predict Outcome in Ebola Virus Disease.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Ebola virus disease (EVD) has a high mortality rate, and while viral load is a known prognostic factor, it is not effective in predicting outcomes across all patients. Exploring host transcriptomic signatures may provide additional predictive value.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Samples were taken for diagnostic purposes during the acute phase of infection from hospitalized patients with Ebola virus (EBOV) collected during the 2013-2016 West African outbreak.
analysis.methods: The transcript abundance of 4 candidate host genes (VCAM1, TUBG1, MS4A4A, ISG15) was quantified by reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) in blood samples. Associations between target gene expression, viral load, and outcome (survival/death) were assessed, and machine learning models were trained and tested to predict patient outcome.
analysis.main_results: EBOV cycle threshold (Ct) values were significantly higher in hospitalized survivors compared to fatalities. During the acute phase, the transcript abundance of VCAM1 and MS4A4A was higher in fatal cases, while TUBG1 expression was elevated in survivors; ISG15 expression did not differ by outcome. In support vector machine models, EBOV Ct alone classified patient outcomes with 86.9% accuracy, while MS4A4A alone reached 82.6%. Combining EBOV Ct with MS4A4A improved prediction to 91.3%. The best-performing model, integrating EBOV Ct, ISG15, and MS4A4A, achieved 100% accuracy in the test set.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Host gene expression markers, particularly MS4A4A, in combination with viral load, improved outcome prediction in EVD beyond viral load alone in ambiguous cases with mid-range Ct values. These findings highlight the utility of host transcript-based assays to inform clinical management and for benchmarking the effectiveness of medical countermeasures during outbreaks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that host transcript-based assays could improve clinical management and help evaluate the effectiveness of medical countermeasures during Ebola virus disease outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to hospitalized patients during a specific outbreak period, and the results may not be generalizable to all EVD cases. The evidence strength is moderate due to the specific context and limited population.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to explore the potential of host transcriptomic signatures to improve outcome prediction in Ebola virus disease (EVD). During the 2013-2016 West African outbreak, transcript abundance of four candidate host genes (VCAM1, TUBG1, MS4A4A, ISG15) was quantified using RT-qPCR in blood samples from hospitalized patients. The results showed that EBOV cycle threshold (Ct) values were significantly higher in survivors compared to fatalities, and transcript levels of VCAM1 and MS4A4A were higher in fatal cases, while TUBG1 was elevated in survivors. Machine learning models using EBOV Ct, MS4A4A, and ISG15 achieved 100% accuracy in predicting patient outcomes. The authors interpreted these findings as indicating that host gene expression markers, particularly MS4A4A, in combination with viral load, can improve outcome prediction in EVD, especially in ambiguous cases with mid-range Ct values. These results suggest that host transcript-based assays could enhance clinical decision-making and help assess medical countermeasures during outbreaks. However, the study was limited to hospitalized patients during a specific outbreak period, which may affect generalizability.

title: Molecular Phenotypes of Sex- and Age-Specific Differences Relating to Outcome in Patients With Ebola Virus Disease.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate age- and sex-specific differences in patients with Ebola virus disease, given the known correlation between viral load and outcome, and the potential influence of age and sex on the course of the disease.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed RNA sequencing data from blood transcriptomes of patients from the 2013-2016 West African Ebola virus outbreak, stratified by age and sex, to correlate with the outcome of infection.
analysis.methods: RNA sequencing was performed on blood samples from patients, and the data were stratified by age and sex to identify molecular differences associated with outcome.
analysis.main_results: The study found that immune responses were downregulated during the acute phase in hospitalized survivors compared to fatal cases, regardless of sex. However, there were differences in the blood transcriptome/host response between females and males and certain age groups.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that age and sex influence the host response to Ebola virus disease, and certain cellular pathways could be targeted to improve survival.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study highlights the importance of considering age and sex in the selection of animal models for Ebola virus disease research and identifies potential therapeutic targets to enhance survival.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the use of previously published data and the potential for confounding factors. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed RNA sequencing data from blood transcriptomes of Ebola virus disease patients, stratified by age and sex, to identify molecular differences associated with outcome. The findings suggest that age and sex influence the host response and could inform future therapeutic strategies.

title: Barriers and Facilitators to Adopting Safe Burial Practices During the 2014–2016 Ebola Virus Disease Outbreak in Liberia: A 2024 Retrospective Mixed-Methods Study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Traditional funeral practices were a significant factor in the transmission of Ebola virus disease (EVD) during the West African outbreak of 2014–2016. Understanding the barriers to and facilitators of adopting safe burial practices is critical for informing future epidemic responses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This mixed-methods study was conducted in Vai and Clara Towns, Monrovia, Liberia. Data collection included surveys (n = 200), in-depth interviews (n = 40), and four focus groups (n = 40) with family members and community leaders.
analysis.methods: Quantitative data was analyzed via descriptive statistics. Thematic analysis was applied to the qualitative data to identify major themes.
analysis.main_results: The survey demonstrated high levels of EVD-related knowledge and perceived risk in 2024; however, these descriptive findings do not establish an association between knowledge and burial behavior. Qualitative analysis revealed seven major themes: cultural and traditional resistance, mistrust and stigma, misinformation, emotional and psychological distress, communication and logistical challenges, socioeconomic constraints, and facilitators of safe practices.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Qualitative findings identified cultural, emotional, social, informational, and logistical factors that influenced the adoption of safe burial practices during the outbreak. The study highlights the importance of addressing these factors in future epidemic responses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Future responses should prioritize early community engagement, the involvement of traditional and religious leaders, culturally sensitive adaptations of protocols, and adequate psychosocial and logistical support. These findings can inform the development of more effective public health strategies for managing outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Knowledge measured in 2024 cannot establish outbreak-era knowledge. The study relies on retrospective accounts, which may introduce bias and limit the accuracy of the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This 2024 retrospective mixed-methods study in Liberia aimed to understand the barriers and facilitators to adopting safe burial practices during the 2014–2016 Ebola virus disease (EVD) outbreak. The study combined surveys, interviews, and focus groups to explore factors influencing burial behavior. Results showed high knowledge of EVD but no direct link to burial practices. Qualitative analysis identified seven themes, including cultural resistance, mistrust, misinformation, and logistical challenges. The study emphasizes the need for culturally sensitive public health strategies, community engagement, and support for traditional leaders. However, the reliance on retrospective data limits the confidence in the findings, as knowledge measured in 2024 cannot reflect outbreak-era understanding. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

title: Whole-genome phylogenetic and population genetic analysis of Orthoebolavirus restonense

analysis.research_question_and_background: Orthoebolavirus restonense (Reston virus; RESTV) is a zoonotic virus detected primarily in non-human primates and swine, yet its evolutionary dynamics and population structure remain poorly understood despite its recognized public health importance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study analyzed 20 publicly available RESTV whole-genome sequences to update phylogenetic relationships, evolutionary timescales, and genetic diversity across host groups and outbreak periods.
analysis.methods: The study conducted in silico analysis of 20 RESTV whole-genome sequences to build upon previous analyses by updating phylogenetic relationships, evolutionary timescales, and incorporating additional analyses of genetic diversity and population subdivision.
analysis.main_results: Maximum-likelihood and Bayesian analyses supported 5 multi-sequence clusters and 2 phylogenetically distinct singleton lineages. The pooled dataset showed high haplotype diversity, with swine-derived genomes exhibiting greater nucleotide diversity than primate-derived genomes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Population structure analyses suggest structured, highly divergent viral sequences, with temporal segregation exerting a greater influence than host-associated factors, although the relative contributions of outbreak period and host are difficult to disentangle.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings raise the possibility of earlier undetected circulation of RESTV and highlight the need for expanded genomic surveillance and One Health integration to better understand its evolution, epidemiology, and zoonotic potential.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The limited number of available genome sequences constrains a comprehensive understanding of RESTV evolutionary history and transmission dynamics, and neutrality tests did not detect evidence of recent rapid population expansion.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted a whole-genome phylogenetic and population genetic analysis of Orthoebolavirus restonense (RESTV) to better understand its evolutionary dynamics and population structure. The researchers analyzed 20 publicly available RESTV sequences using in silico methods, updating phylogenetic relationships and incorporating genetic diversity analyses across host groups and outbreak periods. The results showed 5 multi-sequence clusters and 2 distinct singleton lineages, with swine-derived genomes displaying greater nucleotide diversity than primate-derived ones. The authors interpreted these findings as suggesting structured, highly divergent viral sequences influenced more by temporal segregation than host-associated factors. The study highlights the potential for earlier undetected circulation of RESTV and underscores the need for expanded genomic surveillance and One Health integration to better understand its evolution and zoonotic potential. However, the limited number of sequences constrains a comprehensive understanding of its evolutionary history and transmission dynamics, and neutrality tests did not detect evidence of recent population expansion.

title: Assessing the Risk for Ebola Virus Disease Outbreak and Health System Response Capacity in Conflict-Affected Sudan

analysis.scope_and_question: Ongoing regional outbreaks in Uganda and the DRC, combined with protracted armed conflict in Sudan since April 2023, increase vulnerability to importation and spread, putting Sudan at risk.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: We reviewed peer-reviewed and grey literature using PubMed, Medline, Google Scholar, WHO, CDC, UNICEF, and UN OCHA reports.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Geographic risk synthesis indicates Darfur is at the highest risk for delayed detection and silent transmission, Kordofan serves as a transmission corridor, and Khartoum faces the highest risk of urban amplification.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Sudan faces a moderate to high EVD outbreak risk due to potential virus importation, a conflict-weakened health system, and mass displacement.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Key priorities: strengthen EWARS in conflict zones, decentralize laboratory capacity, restore health facilities with strong IPC, build workforce capacity, and adopt mobility-informed preparedness.

analysis.summary_en: Ongoing regional outbreaks in Uganda and the DRC, combined with protracted armed conflict in Sudan since April 2023, increase vulnerability to importation and spread, putting Sudan at risk. We reviewed peer-reviewed and grey literature using PubMed, Medline, Google Scholar, WHO, CDC, UNICEF, and UN OCHA reports. Geographic risk synthesis indicates Darfur is at the highest risk for delayed detection and silent transmission, Kordofan serves as a transmission corridor, and Khartoum faces the highest risk of urban amplification. Sudan faces a moderate to high EVD outbreak risk due to potential virus importation, a conflict-weakened health system, and mass displacement. Key priorities: strengthen EWARS in conflict zones, decentralize laboratory capacity, restore health facilities with strong IPC, build workforce capacity, and adopt mobility-informed preparedness.

title: Bundibugyo Virus Disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda: A Neglected Public Health Threat

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need to recognize Bundibugyo virus disease as a neglected public health threat in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, highlighting its status as an emerging infectious disease and viral hemorrhagic fever.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study focuses on Bundibugyo virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, examining its epidemiological and clinical characteristics in these regions.
analysis.methods: The methods involve reviewing existing literature and data on Bundibugyo virus disease, with an emphasis on its occurrence and impact in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda.
analysis.main_results: The study reports that Bundibugyo virus disease is a significant and under-recognized public health issue in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, with cases of viral hemorrhagic fever documented.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as evidence of the ongoing threat posed by Bundibugyo virus disease, emphasizing its role as an emerging infectious disease and the need for increased attention.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the importance of improving surveillance and response strategies for Bundibugyo virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda to mitigate its public health impact.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on existing literature and does not include new data, which limits the strength of the evidence. However, it provides a comprehensive overview of the current understanding of Bundibugyo virus disease.

title: Exploratory network-based modelling of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease importation and spread in Uganda using Displacement Tracking Matrix flow data

analysis.research_question_and_background: The 2026 Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in Uganda, linked to the ongoing epidemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), spread through human mobility across borders and within the country. Existing modelling has provided regional level importation estimates but not district level operational guidance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We developed an exploratory, scenario based decision support model to characterise subnational importation and spread patterns using a directed, weighted mobility network constructed from International Organization for Migration (IOM) Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) flows and the 2024 Uganda census data.
analysis.methods: We simulated a stochastic metapopulation SEIR model over 90 days across 135 Ugandan districts and two DRC provinces, performing global sensitivity analysis using Morris elementary-effects screening and total order Sobol indices.
analysis.main_results: The mobility network was sparse (density 0.11), highly unequal (Gini 0.67), and modular (0.50). Kisoro had the highest import risk (in-strength 3,823) and export risk (out-strength 1,350). Under all three scenarios, the model projected similar cumulative case counts (median 20 to 21; pairwise Mann Whitney p < 0.05).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Under the containment assumptions of the model, rapid implementation was associated with substantial containment, but this is scenario-specific and does not imply that NPIs are unnecessary. These projections should be treated as exploratory and require prospective field-based validation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Border surveillance, nationwide preparedness, and community engagement remain essential. The model provides district-level insights for operational guidance in managing Ebola virus disease importation and spread.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The model is exploratory and requires prospective field-based validation. Design limitations include the use of sparse and unequal mobility data, which may affect the accuracy of the projections.

analysis.summary_en: The study developed a decision support model to predict Ebola virus disease importation and spread at the district level in Uganda using mobility data. The model projected similar case counts under different scenarios and highlighted the importance of rapid implementation and ongoing surveillance.

title: Resurgence of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo: Lessons Learned and Future Directions.

analysis.scope_and_question: The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) remains the global epicenter of Ebola virus disease (EVD), having experienced more than 15 outbreaks since the disease was first identified in 1976.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This perspective synthesizes evidence from publicly available reports, epidemiological updates, genomic surveillance findings, and guidance from national and international public health agencies to examine the epidemiological characteristics, health system challenges, response interventions, and lessons learned from the 2025 Ebola outbreak in the DRC.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The 2025 Ebola outbreak demonstrates the continued threat of recurrent EVD in the DRC and underscores the need for resilient surveillance systems, decentralized laboratory capacity, sustained infection prevention and control measures, healthcare worker protection, meaningful community engagement, and strengthened regional collaboration.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Delayed diagnosis due to limited laboratory capacity, reagent shortages, and slow sample transportation impeded timely case confirmation. The outbreak overwhelmed fragile health systems, with inadequate isolation facilities and personal protective equipment contributing to healthcare worker infections, which accounted for 10% of reported cases.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Coordinated national and international interventions, including emergency response activation, ring vaccination with the rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP (Ervebo) vaccine, enhanced surveillance, contact tracing, infection prevention and control measures, and technical support from global partners, were instrumental in interrupting transmission. Integrating genomic surveillance and advancing vaccine research will be critical for improving epidemic preparedness and strengthening health security across Central Africa.

analysis.summary_en: This review article examines the 2025 Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), emphasizing the persistent challenges in outbreak preparedness and response. The outbreak, caused by Zaire ebolavirus, resulted in over 60 confirmed cases and a case fatality rate exceeding 65%. Key factors contributing to the outbreak included viral persistence in human reservoirs, sociocultural practices such as unsafe burial customs, and vaccine hesitancy. The review highlights the critical role of coordinated interventions, including ring vaccination with the Ervebo vaccine, enhanced surveillance, and community engagement, in interrupting transmission. It also underscores the need for resilient health systems, decentralized laboratory capacity, and improved infection prevention measures. The article concludes that genomic surveillance and vaccine research are essential for future epidemic preparedness in the region.

title: Targeting TMEM16F‐Driven Membrane Remodeling: A Promising Strategy for Broad-Spectrum Antiviral Development

analysis.research_question_and_background: The continuous rise of epidemics with potential for global threats necessitates the development of antiviral drugs. Most approved drugs are direct-acting agents (DAAs) targeting specific viral proteins, which restricts their applications. Research on host-directed agents (HDAs) targeting host processes for broad-spectrum antiviral strategies is needed, especially since HDAs are more resistant to viral mutations.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study aims to explore the potential of targeting TMEM16F, a cell membrane Ca2+-activated scramblase, for broad-spectrum antiviral development. TMEM16F’s role in phosphatidylserine (PS) translocation is essential for microvesicle secretion and can be hijacked by viruses for viral spread and immune evasion.
analysis.methods: TMEM16F’s 3D structure was resolved with cryo-electron microscopy, and niclosamide, an FDA-approved anthelminthic drug, was found to inhibit TMEM16F scramblase activity. Drug screening revealed antiviral activity against SARS-CoV-2, and AI-driven drug analog design may be used to optimize niclosamide’s efficacy and minimize cytotoxicity.
analysis.main_results: Niclosamide inhibits TMEM16F scramblase activity and shows antiviral activity against SARS-CoV-2. However, niclosamide has low bioavailability and can cause severe side effects at high dosage.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: TMEM16F’s role in viral spread and immune evasion is crucial, and targeting its scramblase activity offers broad-spectrum antiviral potential. Niclosamide can be repurposed and optimized as a pan-viral HDA.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Targeting TMEM16F scramblase activity could provide a broad-spectrum antiviral strategy. Further research is needed to identify strategic host targets and optimize niclosamide for clinical use.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the low bioavailability and potential side effects of niclosamide. The extent to which different virus families utilize TMEM16F for viral spread and immune evasion remains to be elucidated.

analysis.summary_en: The study explores the potential of targeting TMEM16F, a cell membrane Ca2+-activated scramblase, for broad-spectrum antiviral development. TMEM16F’s role in viral spread and immune evasion is crucial, and targeting its scramblase activity offers broad-spectrum antiviral potential. Niclosamide, an FDA-approved anthelminthic drug, inhibits TMEM16F scramblase activity and shows antiviral activity against SARS-CoV-2, but further research is needed to optimize its efficacy and minimize side effects.

title: The vaccination paradox: how East Africa’s success in Ebola vaccine preparedness may be creating new public expectations for future outbreaks

analysis.research_question_and_background: The framework draws on expectation-disconfirmation and crisis and emergency risk communication theories and distinguishes established evidence from interpretation and testable hypotheses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: DiscussionWe do not intend the vaccination paradox to weaken the case for Ebola vaccines; if anything, we read it as strengthening that case, since vaccines remain among the most important tools in Ebola preparedness.
analysis.methods: We are not aware of prior work that integrates these four literatures around the specific question of cross-species vaccine expectations in Ebola preparedness, which is the gap this Perspective attempts to address; again, this is our reading of a non-systematic search rather than a systematic bibliometric claim.
analysis.main_results: We recommend that reviewers, editors and readers treat these hypotheses as a research agenda rather than as demonstrated preparedness risks.Table 1The vaccine expectation gap framework for Ebola preparedness in East Africa.Preparedness domainCurrent achievement (documented)Emerging paradox (proposed)Strategic response (recommended)Evidentiary statusVaccine scienceLicensed vaccines exist for Zaire ebolavirus diseaseProtection may be assumed by some audiences to cover all ebolavirus diseasePromote species-specific vaccine literacyAchievement: established finding.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: We use “Ebola virus disease” specifically for disease caused by Zaire ebolavirus, “Sudan virus disease” and “Bundibugyo virus disease” for disease caused by those respective species, and “ebolavirus disease” or “Ebola disease” as the broader umbrella term covering any recognized ebolavirus species, following current WHO usage (3).Whether members of the public distinguish between ebolavirus species, and whether successful vaccination against one species generates expectations of availability against others, are empirical questions that, to our knowledge, have not yet been directly studied in East or Central Africa.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Domains may overlap in practice and should be adapted to local outbreak histories, vaccine availability and community communication needs.Figure 1Revised conceptual framework of the Vaccine Expectation Gap in Ebola preparedness, distinguishing documented relationships from proposed, hypothesized relationships.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: We suggest that the next phase of Ebola vaccine preparedness research in East and Central Africa should test, empirically, whether combining better vaccines with deliberate expectation governance improves community trust when the next outbreak, of whichever ebolavirus species, arrives.

analysis.summary_en: The framework draws on expectation-disconfirmation and crisis and emergency risk communication theories and distinguishes established evidence from interpretation and testable hypotheses. DiscussionWe do not intend the vaccination paradox to weaken the case for Ebola vaccines; if anything, we read it as strengthening that case, since vaccines remain among the most important tools in Ebola preparedness. We are not aware of prior work that integrates these four literatures around the specific question of cross-species vaccine expectations in Ebola preparedness, which is the gap this Perspective attempts to address; again, this is our reading of a non-systematic search rather than a systematic bibliometric claim. We recommend that reviewers, editors and readers treat these hypotheses as a research agenda rather than as demonstrated preparedness risks.Table 1The vaccine expectation gap framework for Ebola preparedness in East Africa.Preparedness domainCurrent achievement (documented)Emerging paradox (proposed)Strategic response (recommended)Evidentiary statusVaccine scienceLicensed vaccines exist for Zaire ebolavirus diseaseProtection may be assumed by some audiences to cover all ebolavirus diseasePromote species-specific vaccine literacyAchievement: established finding.
